findings.title: Italian text placed in Lithuanian translation file (loginTotpStep1)
findings.body: The loginTotpStep1 value was changed from a Lithuanian sentence beginning with 'Įdiekite' to Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. This is the wrong language for the lt (Lithuanian) messages file. Lithuanian users of the login UI will see the Italian sentence instead of a localized one, which is a regression versus the prior Lithuanian content (e.g. a proper translation would start with 'Įdiekite').

findings.title: RuntimeException on missing English reference aborts whole verification
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() computes the English reference path by replacing 'resources-community' with 'resources' and the language suffix with '_en.properties'. When the resulting English file does not exist (for example, when only a translations file exists in resources-community and no English counterpart lives in resources/), new FileInputStream(englishFile) throws IOException which is wrapped in a RuntimeException. This RuntimeException is not caught by the try-catch in verify() (which only handles IOException), so it propagates out of verify() and aborts the Maven build entirely - including the duplicate-key checks that already ran successfully for that file. The sanitizer should at minimum catch this and record a message rather than failing the build.

findings.title: Matcher state is stale after value is reassigned in santizeAnchors
findings.body: In santizeAnchors(), the matcher is created against the value at method entry: `Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)`. Inside the while loop, `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` reassigns the local `value` variable, but the matcher continues to operate on the ORIGINAL character sequence it was bound to at construction time. On the next iteration, matcher.find() continues scanning the ORIGINAL value while value.replaceFirst(...) acts on the (already-modified) current value. This divergence can cause: (a) the wrong occurrence of an anchor being removed when value contains multiple copies of the same anchor, (b) stale positions when anchors shift after previous removals, and (c) the loop iterating past anchors that were already removed from the current value. The matcher needs to be recreated (or `value` re-assigned to a freshly-built matcher) after each replaceFirst.

findings.title: Typo in method name 'santizeAnchors'
findings.body: The method name is spelled 'santizeAnchors' (missing the 'i' in 'sanitize'). It should be 'sanitizeAnchors'.
